text:
The 30-year costs more in total interest, typically about twice as much or more. For example, $300,000 at 6%: roughly $155,700 in interest over 15 years versus $347,500 over 30. The 30-year has the lower monthly payment ($1,799 vs. $2,532), but the balance stays outstanding far longer.

In practice the gap is usually wider, since 30-year loans generally carry a higher rate than 15-year loans.
